summary: Iter 221 — Implementer Workload Summary tooltip (Panel de Proyectos) tested end-to-end. Backend endpoint GET /api/projects/implementers/{user_id}/workload-summary verified for shape, resilience (zeros for nonexistent id), auth requirement, and data precision (projects_count matches active projects only). Frontend hover tooltip on /projects verified: 90 triggers render, popover opens on hover with 4 labeled metrics + progress bar, fetch happens on open (200 OK), popover closes on mouseleave, caching works (no refetch on re-hover same name), and 'Sin asignar' is plain text without hover trigger.

design_issues.screen: Projects table (pre-existing, not introduced by Iter221)
issues: React hydration warnings: <span data-ve-dynamic="true" style="display:contents"> wrapper is rendered as a direct child of <tbody>/<tr>, which is invalid HTML and causes hydration noise. This belongs to an external instrumentation wrapper (x-ve-dynamic), not to ImplementerWorkloadHover, but it pollutes the console on the Projects page.

critical_code_review_comments: ImplementerWorkloadHover.jsx: clean, small (~100 lines), uses HoverCard with openDelay=300 / closeDelay=80, fetches on open, caches via local state (per-instance — each row has its own ImplementerWorkloadHover so cache is per-trigger, not per-user-id globally). If perf becomes a concern (e.g. opening the same user across rows), a module-level Map keyed by userId would avoid repeat network calls across different rows for the same implementer. Current per-instance cache still prevents re-fetch on re-hovering the SAME row (verified).

Backend implementer_workload_summary uses cajas_pendientes = max(0, cajas_asignadas - cajas_configuradas) per project then sums — symmetric with PVV. Returns int 0 for nonexistent users (no 404), which matches the requested resilience contract for the tooltip use-case.
routes/projects.py is ~4072 lines — exceeds the 700-line guideline; consider splitting (out of scope for this iteration).
test_credentials: rgonzalez@megasoft.com.ve / admin123 (admin). Login returns 'session_token' used as Bearer.
